section: Management's Discussion and Analysis — Product Prices
excerpt: The Company's realized product pricing is reflective of the prevailing benchmark pricing.
interpretation: OUR INTERPRETATION (not issuer text): Management statement that realized prices follow benchmarks. It establishes the transmission from WTI/Brent to revenue, not its size.

section: Management's Discussion and Analysis — Summary of Quarterly Financial Results
excerpt: Crude oil pricing – Fluctuations in global supply/demand including crude oil production levels from OPEC+ and its impact on world supply, the impact of geopolitical and market uncertainties (including those due to the conflicts in the Middle East, Ukraine and Venezuela, and the impacts of ongoing tariff and trade uncertainty) on worldwide benchmark pricing, the impact of shale oil production in North America, the impact of the start-up of the Trans Mountain Expansion ("TMX") pipeline in 2024, the impact of the WCS Heavy Differential from WTI in North America, and the impact of the differential between WTI and Brent benchmark pricing in the International segments.
interpretation: OUR INTERPRETATION (not issuer text): Management attributes quarterly net-earnings volatility first to crude oil pricing, naming both the WCS-WTI and WTI-Brent differentials. This is about earnings volatility, not share-price behaviour.

section: Management's Discussion and Analysis — Business Environment — Benchmark Commodity Prices
excerpt: Substantially all of the Company's production is sold based on US dollar benchmark pricing, with crude oil marketed based on WTI and Brent indices, and natural gas marketed using a diversified mix of AECO- and NYMEX-based pricing.
interpretation: OUR INTERPRETATION (not issuer text): Direct price channel: crude revenue is indexed to WTI and Brent in US dollars, so realized prices in C$ also depend on USD/CAD (the next sentence on the page says so).

section: Management's Discussion and Analysis — Business Environment — Benchmark Commodity Prices (table)
excerpt: WTI benchmark price (US$/bbl) $ 64.77 $ 75.72 $ 77.61 Dated Brent benchmark price (US$/bbl) $ 69.02 $ 80.75 $ 82.61 WCS Heavy Differential from WTI (US$/bbl) $ 11.10 $ 14.73 $ 18.62
interpretation: OUR INTERPRETATION (not issuer text): Disclosed benchmark levels. Our arithmetic: WTI fell US$10.95 (-14%) while the WCS discount narrowed US$3.63, so heavy-oil realizations fell less than WTI.

section: Management's Discussion and Analysis — Business Environment — Benchmark Commodity Prices
excerpt: The WCS Heavy Differential averaged US$11.10 per bbl for 2025 compared with US$14.73 per bbl for 2024 (2023 – US$18.62 per bbl). The narrowing of the WCS Heavy Differential for 2025 from 2024 primarily reflected full year takeaway capacity on the TMX pipeline and strong US Gulf Coast heavy oil pricing.
interpretation: OUR INTERPRETATION (not issuer text): Company-stated cause of the narrower differential: TMX pipeline capacity and US Gulf Coast heavy-oil demand. Infrastructure, not just the WTI level, drives Canadian heavy-oil realizations.

section: Management's Discussion and Analysis — Realized Product Prices – Exploration and Production — North America
excerpt: North America realized crude oil and NGLs prices decreased 7% to average $70.90 per bbl for 2025 from $76.37 per bbl for 2024 (2023 – $70.51 per bbl), primarily reflecting lower WTI benchmark pricing, partially offset by a narrowing of the WCS Heavy Differential.
interpretation: OUR INTERPRETATION (not issuer text): Both channels at work in one sentence: realized C$ prices fell 7% versus a 14% fall in US$ WTI, with the narrower WCS discount (and FX) cushioning the decline.

section: Management's Discussion and Analysis — Other — Sensitivity Analysis
interpretation: OUR INTERPRETATION (not issuer text): Strongest quantitative disclosure in the batch: a US$1.00/bbl change in WTI changes annualized operating cash flow and net earnings by about $409 million each. This is operating sensitivity on Q4 2025 volumes, not a share-price beta.

section: Note 18 Financial Instruments — Financial Risk Factors — a) Market risk — Commodity price risk management
excerpt: The Company periodically uses commodity derivative financial instruments to manage its exposure to commodity price risk associated with the sale of its future crude oil and natural gas production, and with natural gas purchases.
interpretation: OUR INTERPRETATION (not issuer text): Possible mitigant. 'Periodically' and the absence of crude-oil contract volumes on this page mean we cannot assume the WTI sensitivity is hedged. The $409M figure excludes mark-to-market on risk management by construction.
